## What this is

One row per capability the project currently asserts. The claim and the check that proves it are CURATED in `lib/ops/capability-registry.ts`. The result beside it is DERIVED, by `lib/ops/status-result.ts`, from a run record an instrument actually wrote — a gate run, a walk run, a reader-suite run, or the post-deploy observer.

**No typed string anywhere can produce a green row.** The registry has no field to write a result into. A capability whose check has no run record renders UNPROVEN; one whose newest record measured a tree this release does not contain renders STALE. Both are facts about our instrumentation, never verdicts on the capability, and neither is softened here.

The four states:

- `PROVEN` — a current run record says the named check passed.
- `FAILING` — a current run record says the named check did not pass.
- `STALE` — a record exists but measured a tree the release does not contain, or names no tested SHA at all.
- `UNPROVEN` — no run record names this check, or no check is named.

`proofClass` is DERIVED too, and derived from WHO RAN IT rather than from how canonical the command was. `INDEPENDENTLY_REPRODUCED` requires all three of: a clean working tree, a tested SHA the integration branch ALREADY contained when the run started, and a runner that is not a local session. Everything else — including every run this session invoked against its own work, and every record written before the provenance block existed — is `SESSION_MEASURED`.

That distinction is the one RULING 216 turns on, and it was wrong until Session B: a passing canonical result was labelled `INDEPENDENTLY_REPRODUCED` unconditionally, which is the class `pnpm gates` earns on an unmerged branch. Only `INDEPENDENTLY_REPRODUCED` production-target results count toward the activation gate, so the strongest class in the repository was being awarded to the weakest evidence for it.

**22 capability row(s) stated — 16 PROVEN, 0 FAILING, 0 STALE, 6 UNPROVEN. The tables below render exactly 22 row(s) in total.**
